name: Custom or hidden cursor
plain: Replaces the mouse pointer with an image, or hides it, inside the page.
meaning: A site can change or hide the pointer, helping games and drawing apps. Browsers block cursors that could imitate system pointers or hide over browser UI, so a page cannot fake the cursor outside its own area.

web.api: CSS cursor: url(img) x y, auto; cursor: none

access.persistence: Per element, while the pointer is over it; no stored state
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Applies to the frame's own content only
steps: Page sets CSS cursor on an element
Browser draws the image while the pointer is over the element
Cursor reverts at the edge or over browser UI

limits.headline: Can swap your mouse pointer for an image, or hide it, only inside the page
limits.user_action: You move your mouse over the page or a button on it.
can: Show a custom image as the pointer
Hide the pointer while it is over the page
Change the pointer for different buttons or areas
cannot: Change the pointer outside the page, in the browser's toolbar or other apps
Use very large images, since browsers cap the size and fall back to the normal pointer
Hide the pointer after you move it out of the page
limits.differs: Phones and tablets have no mouse pointer, so touch screens ignore this.

story.what_it_is: A page swaps your mouse pointer for its own picture, or hides it.

marketing.name: CSS cursor
marketing.pitch: Shows how a page can use built in pointer shapes or its own image for the pointer.

story.for_you: You see the pointer change into a hand, a crosshair, a paint brush or a game sword. Sometimes it vanishes so you can look around a 3D scene.
story.for_makers: A custom pointer makes a site feel like an app and tells you what a click will do. It is used for polish and for games. It can also be abused to hide the real pointer position in tricks.

use_cases.example: A first person browser shooter hides the pointer and locks it in place so moving the mouse turns your view.
A design board shows each teammate's name next to their own colored pointer as they move around the canvas.
A drawing tool turns the pointer into a circle that matches your brush size.
A flashy brand site turns the pointer into a logo or a follow along shape to feel playful.
A scam page hides the real pointer and draws a fake one a few pixels off so clicks land on a hidden button.
A site enlarges the pointer for people with low vision.
A kids learning game turns the pointer into a friendly animal or star.

technical_bounds: Image size limit is 128 by 128 px in Chrome and Firefox (32 by 32 recommended); larger images are ignored
Chrome blocks cursors larger than 32 by 32 px when they would overlap browser UI (about 2019)
Cursors only change inside the viewport; the cursor cannot be moved by script (see Pointer Lock for hidden relative motion)
cursor: none hides the pointer; the person can still see it over browser UI

abuse: Fake cursor positioned away from the true pointer (clickjacking aid)

history.change: Large custom cursors are blocked when they would overlap browser UI
